mainTopic: Offspring and nursing of a טרפה, redeeming holy animals that became טרפה, and the start of the משנה contrasting קדשי מזבח with קדשי בדק הבית
overview: The משנה says רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring of a טרפה on the מזבח, while the חכמים allow it. The גמרא explains the case in two ways. If a טרפה can give birth, the argument is about זה וזה גורם. If it cannot, the argument is about whether a fetus is part of its mother (עובר ירך אמו). רב הונא says even the חכמים forbid a chick from a טרפה's egg, and רבא tries to support him from a ברייתא about worms. אביי reads that ברייתא the other way and brings an explicit ברייתא that even רבי אליעזר permits the chick, and רבא accepts it. Next, the גמרא explains that a kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה is unfit only when it lived on that milk a full day at a time. It then brings the source for not redeeming holy animals that became טרפה just to feed dogs, along with a second version that allows it. The פרק ends, and a new משנה begins listing rules that apply to קדשי מזבח but not to קדשי בדק הבית, starting with תמורה and with פיגול, נותר and טומאה.

steps.title: First view: the טרפה became pregnant after becoming a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the offspring of a טרפה. It explains that, according to the view that a טרפה can give birth, the case is an animal that became a טרפה first and got pregnant afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The offspring of a טרפה...' According to the one who says a טרפה can give birth, you find this case when the animal became a טרפה and only later got pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about the offspring of a טרפה and starts explaining exactly what case the מחלוקת is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an outside question of whether a טרפה can get pregnant and give birth. If it can, the simplest case is one where the mother was already a טרפה when she conceived. The גמרא does not give the reason for the מחלוקת yet; that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect; it is forbidden to eat and cannot be brought on the מזבח
Offspring, the baby animal
You find it, meaning this is the case we are talking about
And afterward, later on

steps.confusionAlert: The printed text has the word אינה in round brackets. Read the line without it: 'according to the one who says a טרפה CAN give birth.' The opposite view comes later, in step 3.

phrases.english: "The offspring of a tereifa, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: רבי אליעזר says it may not be offered on the מזבח, and the חכמים say it may.

phrases.english: According to the one who says a tereifa can give birth,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Without it, the line means a טרפה is able to give birth.

phrases.english: you find it in a case where it became a tereifa
and afterward became pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה יָלְדָה מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the view that a טרפה can give birth, the משנה's case is an animal that became a טרפה before it got pregnant.

steps.title: The argument is about two causes, one forbidden and one permitted
steps.stepSummary: In this case, the מחלוקת depends on זה וזה גורם. רבי אליעזר holds that something produced by a forbidden cause and a permitted cause together is forbidden. The חכמים hold that it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they argue about: רבי אליעזר holds that when this and that both cause something, it is forbidden. The חכמים hold that when this and that both cause something, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the argument in the case from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby comes from two parents: a mother that is a טרפה (forbidden) and a father that is fine (permitted). רבי אליעזר says the forbidden part makes the baby forbidden. The חכמים say the permitted part allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that both cause it: something produced by a forbidden factor and a permitted factor together
And this is what they argue about
Forbidden
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: זה וזה גורם is a general rule that appears in many places in ש״ס. Here it is applied to a baby animal with one forbidden parent and one permitted parent.

phrases.english: And in this they disagree:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds: when this and that both cause something, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: 'This and that' are the two parents: the טרפה mother, which is forbidden, and the healthy father, which is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: when this and that both cause something, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the case set up in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: זה וזה גורם is forbidden. חכמים: זה וזה גורם is permitted.

steps.title: Second view: the animal became a טרפה while pregnant
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that a טרפה cannot live long enough to give birth, the case is an animal that got pregnant first and then became a טרפה. Here the מחלוקת is whether a fetus counts as part of its mother's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says a טרפה cannot live, you find this case when the animal got pregnant and only later became a טרפה. And this is what they argue about: רבי אליעזר holds that a fetus is like its mother's thigh, and the חכמים hold that a fetus is not like its mother's thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain the משנה, following the opposite view about whether a טרפה can give birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טרפה cannot get pregnant and give birth, then the only possible case is a mother that was already pregnant when she became a טרפה. Now the question is not about two parents. It is whether the fetus is simply a limb of the mother, so that it is a טרפה like her. רבי אליעזר says yes, so it is forbidden. The חכמים say no, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot live, meaning it cannot survive long enough to give birth
A fetus is like its mother's thigh, meaning it is part of the mother's body
Fetus

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the משנה. (1) The mother became a טרפה first and got pregnant later: the argument is about זה וזה גורם. (2) The mother got pregnant first and became a טרפה later: the argument is about עובר ירך אמו.

phrases.english: According to the one who says a tereifa cannot live,
you find it in a case where it became pregnant
and afterward became a tereifa.
And in this they disagree:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר עוּבָּר יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds a fetus is the thigh of its mother,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי עוּבָּר לָאו יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold a fetus is not the thigh of its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵיפָה אֵינָהּ חַיָּה מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of the משנה's case, based on the opposite view from steps 1-2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the mother got pregnant before becoming a טרפה, רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring because עובר ירך אמו, and the חכמים permit it because עובר לאו ירך אמו.

steps.title: רב הונא: the חכמים agree about a chick from a טרפה's egg
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that even the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר that a chick hatched from the egg of a טרפה bird is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about a chick from the egg of a טרפה, that it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a new case where the חכמים do not argue: a chick that hatches from a טרפה bird's egg is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים permitted the offspring of a טרפה animal. רב הונא limits that ruling: it does not cover a chick that hatched from a טרפה's egg. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree
A chick
An egg
The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי אליעזר in the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Eliezer
regarding a chick from the egg of a tereifa, that it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the חכמים's lenient ruling from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the חכמים forbid a chick that hatched from the egg of a טרפה.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים agree here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב הונא's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים would be strict here. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים permitted the offspring of a טרפה animal. So it seems strange that they would forbid the offspring of a טרפה bird. The גמרא wants to know what makes the two cases different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב הונא's statement in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים, who permit the offspring of a טרפה animal, forbid a chick from a טרפה's egg

steps.title: A fetus grows in its own space, but an egg grows from the hen's body
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים permitted only the offspring of an animal, because it grows in its own space. An egg grows out of the hen's own body, so even the חכמים agree that the chick is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים only argue with רבי אליעזר about the offspring of an animal, because it grows from the air, its own space. But the egg of a טרפה grows from the body of the hen itself, so even the חכמים agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by showing how an animal fetus is different from an egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal fetus develops as its own separate being, even while inside the mother. That is why the חכמים do not treat it as part of the טרפה. An egg is formed from the hen's own body, so it is really part of the forbidden mother, and the chick inside it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argued up to here, meaning their argument is limited to this case
It grows from the air, meaning in its own separate space
From its body
A hen

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, the חכמים's lenient ruling applies only to an animal fetus, which grows as its own separate being. A chick from a טרפה's egg would be forbidden by everyone, because the egg grows from the mother's own body. Steps 8-10 challenge this view.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים changed their view. They still permit the offspring of a טרפה animal. A bird's egg is simply a different case, because it is formed from the mother's body.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: The Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer only
regarding the offspring of an animal,
which grows from the air,
phrases.notes: 'From the air' means in its own space: even inside the mother, the fetus grows as a separate being.

phrases.english: but the egg of a tereifa,
which grows from the body of the hen,
even the Rabbis concede.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An animal fetus grows in its own space, so the חכמים do not treat it as part of the טרפה mother. An egg grows from the hen's body, so the chick is forbidden even according to the חכמים.

steps.title: רבא supports רב הונא from the case of worms
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites a ברייתא where the חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר about worms from a living person. He reads it to mean they argue only because worms are just a secretion, while an egg is part of the hen's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב הונא: A ברייתא supports you. A full ladle of worms that came from a living person: רבי אליעזר says it is impure, and the חכמים say it is pure. The חכמים argue only about worms, which are just a secretion. But an egg comes from the hen's own body, so even the חכמים agree it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to back up רב הונא's rule that even the חכמים forbid a chick from a טרפה's egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the חכמים say worms that left a living person are not like corpse matter, because worms are only a secretion and not really part of the body. רבא reasons that an egg is different, since it comes from the hen's own body. So even the חכמים would treat it as part of the טרפה hen.

keyTerms.meaning: A ladle. A ladleful of corpse dust is the amount that makes things טָמֵא.
Worms or maggots
A secretion, waste that comes out of the body
Rules it impure / rules it pure

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Huna:
There is a baraita that supports you:
A full ladle of worms
phrases.notes: A ladleful is the amount of dust from a dead body that makes things impure.

phrases.english: that came from a living person
Rabbi Eliezer rules it impure,
and the Rabbis rule it pure.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ
phrases.english: The Rabbis disagree with him only
about worms,
which are merely a secretion.
But an egg,
which comes from the hen's own body,
even the Rabbis agree.
phrases.notes: They agree with רבי אליעזר that the chick from a טרפה's egg is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for רב הונא's view explained in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that even the חכמים forbid a chick from a טרפה's egg
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a ladleful of worms from a living person, read as limiting the חכמים' leniency to a mere secretion

steps.title: אביי turns the worm proof the other way
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the opposite makes more sense. רבי אליעזר is strict only with worms, because a living person is called a worm. An egg rots into plain dirt before the chick grows, so even רבי אליעזר would permit the chick.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: On the contrary, the opposite makes sense. רבי אליעזר argues with the חכמים only about worms, because a living person is called a 'worm,' as it says: 'And the hope of man is a worm, and the son of man a maggot.' But with an egg, when does the chick grow? When the egg rots. Once it rots it is just dirt, so even רבי אליעזר agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's proof by reading the same ברייתא in the reverse direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read the ברייתא as showing how far the חכמים are lenient. אביי reads it as showing how far רבי אליעזר is strict: he is strict only with worms, because a פסוק links people to worms. A chick grows only after the egg rots into plain dirt, so it is no longer tied to the טרפה hen, and even רבי אליעזר would permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
The opposite makes more sense
It rots or decays
Just plain dirt

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבא and אביי read the same ברייתא. רבא focuses on where the חכמים are lenient, and אביי focuses on where רבי אליעזר is strict. They reach opposite results about the egg.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
On the contrary, the opposite makes sense:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer disagrees
with the Rabbis only about worms,
because a person is called a 'worm' while he is still alive,
as it is written: 'And the hope of man is a worm,'
and the son of man a maggot.'
But with an egg,
when does the chick grow?
When the egg rots.
And once it has rotted,
it is just dirt,
so even Rabbi Eliezer agrees!
phrases.notes: He would agree that the chick is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof by reading the same ברייתא the opposite way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the worm ברייתא, and also רב הונא's conclusion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא limits רבי אליעזר's strictness, not the חכמים' leniency. An egg turns into plain dirt before the chick grows.

steps.title: A ברייתא says outright that the chick is permitted
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a ברייתא that says clearly that רבי אליעזר agrees the chick from a טרפה's egg is permitted. This goes directly against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, a ברייתא says it clearly: רבי אליעזר agrees with the חכמים that a chick from the egg of a טרפה is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a second, stronger point: a ברייתא that openly says the opposite of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the debate was about reasoning. Now there is an explicit source saying that even the strict opinion, רבי אליעזר, permits the chick. That leaves no room for רב הונא's claim that even the חכמים forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, adding another point
Explicitly, openly

phrases.english: And furthermore, a baraita teaches it explicitly:
Rabbi Eliezer agrees with the Rabbis
that a chick from a טרפה's egg is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens אביי's rejection with an explicit source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that even the חכמים forbid the chick
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says that even רבי אליעזר permits the chick, so it cannot be that everyone forbids it.

steps.title: רבא accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא admits that if a ברייתא says this, he accepts it, and his support for רב הונא falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is taught in a ברייתא, then it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives in. An explicit ברייתא beats his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not argue against the source. He accepts that a chick from a טרפה's egg is permitted, at least according to this ברייתא, and his support for רב הונא is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: If a ברייתא teaches it, it is taught, and I accept it

steps.whatToRemember: The worm ברייתא can be read either way. In the end, an explicit ברייתא says even רבי אליעזר permits a chick from a טרפה's egg, which goes against רב הונא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If it is taught, it is taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the ברייתא brought in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The explicit ברייתא decides it: a chick from a טרפה's egg is permitted, even according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Why does רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס disqualify the nursing animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks for the reason behind רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's ruling about a kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: A kosher animal (that nursed from a טרפה is disqualified from the altar). What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה and asks for its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה cannot be brought on the מזבח. The גמרא wants to know what makes it unfit, since the animal itself is healthy and kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher, unblemished animal
Etc. The rest of the משנה's line is assumed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
A kosher animal, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה's full line: a kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה is unfit for the מזבח.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a kosher animal that nursed from a טרפה is disqualified

steps.title: Fattening can't be the reason, because of the idol-feed case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is that the animal grew fat from the טרפה's milk. It rejects this by pointing to an animal fed with idol-worship feed, which is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because the animal was fattened from the טרפה, then if someone fed it vetches of idol worship, would it also be forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible reason and immediately attacks it with a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested reason is that the animal's body grew from forbidden food. But an animal that ate forbidden idol-worship feed is not made unfit just from eating it. So getting fat from something forbidden cannot be the reason. The next step gives the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Was fattened
But if so, introducing an unacceptable result
Vetches, a plant used as animal feed
Idol worship

phrases.english: If you say it is because it was fattened from it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the טרפה whose milk the kosher animal drank.

phrases.english: then if so,
if someone fed it vetches of idol worship,
would it also be forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 11's question and knocks it down.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested reason that the animal is unfit because it was fattened from the טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If eating something forbidden made an animal unfit, then an animal fed idol-worship vetches would be forbidden too, and it is not.

steps.title: The real case: the animal lived a full day at a time on the טרפה's milk
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא טריטאה explains that the משנה means a kosher animal that nursed fresh milk from the טרפה every morning. Since that milk kept it going for a whole day each time, its life depended on the טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי חנינא טריטאה taught before רבי יוחנן: the case is where the animal nursed warm milk from the טרפה every morning. Since it could survive on that milk for a full day, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's ruling, after the 'it got fat' reason was rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting fat from forbidden food is not enough to forbid an animal, as we saw from the animal fed with עבודה זרה feed. So the גמרא narrows the case. Here the kosher animal lived on the טרפה's milk for a full day each time, so its very survival came from the טרפה. That is what makes it unfit for the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'boiling milk': warm, fresh milk straight from the animal
From morning to morning: once every day
A full twenty-four-hour period

steps.whatToRemember: The kosher animal is forbidden only when the טרפה's milk kept it alive day after day. Just growing fat from forbidden food does not forbid an animal.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Ḥanina Terita taught
before Rabbi Yoḥanan:
for example, where one let it nurse warm milk
phrases.notes: 'It' is the kosher animal, and the milk comes from the טרפה.

phrases.english: every morning, from one morning to the next,
since it can survive on it
for a full twenty-four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, תָּנֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא טְרִיטָאָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected 'it got fat' reason from step 12 with a narrower case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason was that the animal grew fat from the טרפה's milk, but that cannot be right.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where the animal's daily survival depended on the טרפה's milk, a full day at a time.

steps.title: Asking for the source that holy animals which became טרפה are not redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, which says holy animals that became טרפה may not be redeemed. It asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: all holy animals that became טרפה may not be redeemed, and so on. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A holy animal with a blemish can usually be redeemed and then eaten as regular meat. A טרפה cannot be eaten at all, so redeeming it would only be useful for feeding dogs. The גמרא wants a source that this is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy animals set aside as קרבנות
Redeem: transfer the holiness onto money so the animal becomes ordinary
From where do we know these words? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: All sacrificial animals that became טרפה
one may not redeem, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of nursing and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for not redeeming holy animals that became טרפה.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that holy animals are not redeemed to feed dogs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק about eating redeemed holy animals word by word: 'slaughter' but not shear, 'eat' but not for your dogs, 'meat' but not milk. From 'eat', and not for your dogs, it learns that we do not redeem holy animals to feed them to dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'You may slaughter', but not shear. 'And eat', but not for your dogs. 'Meat', but not milk. From here we learn that holy animals are not redeemed to feed them to dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that gets the rule from the words of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק allows redeemed holy animals only for slaughtering and eating meat. Each word rules something out: shearing, giving to dogs, and milk. Since a טרפה can only go to dogs, there is no point in redeeming it, so it is not redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: Shearing wool
Meat
To feed them to dogs

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule: redemption is allowed only so that people can eat the meat, not for lower uses like feeding dogs.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'You may slaughter', but not shearing,
'and eat', but not for your dogs,
'meat', but not milk.
From here we learn that one does not redeem sacrificial animals
to feed them to dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'and eat' in דברים 12:15 excludes feeding to dogs, so holy animals are not redeemed for that purpose.

steps.title: A second version reads the פסוק differently and allows redeeming for dogs
steps.stepSummary: Some report the ברייתא differently: 'slaughter and eat' teaches only that benefit is allowed from the time of slaughter onward. Feeding dogs comes after slaughter, so this תנא holds that holy animals may be redeemed to feed them to dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: 'You may slaughter and eat' means you may benefit from them only from the time of slaughter onward. This תנא holds that holy animals may be redeemed to feed them to dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the ברייתא, which leads to the opposite ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the פסוק is read as one phrase about timing. It forbids benefits from a living animal, like wool and milk, but allows anything after slaughter. Feeding the meat to dogs happens after slaughter, so it is allowed, and this goes against what the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission
From the time of slaughter and onward
He holds: introduces the opinion that follows from what was said

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the same פסוק. The first reads 'and eat' as excluding dogs. The second reads the words as being only about timing, so dogs are fine after slaughter.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
'You may slaughter and eat':
you have no permission to benefit from them
except from the time of slaughter and onward,
so he holds: one may redeem sacrificial animals
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of this second version of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: to feed them to dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the ברייתא from step 15, with the opposite ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per this version, only benefits from a living animal are excluded, so one may redeem holy animals to feed them to dogs.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the פרק כל האסורין
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק כל האסורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק כל האסורין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said at the end of each פרק to show we hope to come back and learn it again. It does not add any new law.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing words said when finishing a פרק
The name of this פרק, taken from its opening words

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק ends with two ideas. An animal whose survival came from a טרפה is unfit for the altar. Holy animals that became טרפה are not redeemed just to feed dogs, though one version of the ברייתא allows it.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'All the forbidden ones'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last discussion.

steps.title: New משנה: Two Kinds of Holy Items Have Different Rules
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens by saying that some rules apply to קדשי מזבח but not to קדשי בדק הבית, and some rules apply to קדשי בדק הבית but not to קדשי מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Some rules apply to items consecrated for the altar but not to items consecrated for Temple upkeep. And some rules apply to items consecrated for Temple upkeep but not to items consecrated for the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a general opening line. It is setting up a list of differences that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of holy things. קדשי מזבח are things set aside to be offered on the altar. קדשי בדק הבית are things given to the Temple treasury for upkeep. The משנה says each kind has its own special rules, and it will now spell them out.

keyTerms.meaning: Items consecrated for the altar, meaning animals set aside as קרבנות
Items consecrated for Temple upkeep. They go to the treasury, not onto the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Both kinds are truly holy (הקדש). The משנה is not saying one of them is less holy. It is saying some specific rules apply to only one of the two kinds.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
There is a rule with items consecrated for the altar
that does not apply to items consecrated for Temple upkeep,
and there is a rule with items consecrated for Temple upkeep
that does not apply to items consecrated for the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁאֵין בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the new פרק after the closing line in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשי מזבח and קדשי בדק הבית each have rules that do not apply to the other.

steps.title: Only Altar Animals Can Create a Substitute
steps.stepSummary: The first difference is that קדשי מזבח create a תמורה, but קדשי בדק הבית do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: For altar items create a substitute, but Temple-upkeep items do not create a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first example of a rule that applies only to קדשי מזבח: the law of תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורה means someone tries to swap a regular animal for a holy one. With קדשי מזבח, the new animal becomes holy too. With קדשי בדק הבית, the swap does nothing, so the other animal stays ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an ordinary animal that someone tries to exchange for a holy animal
They make a substitute, meaning the exchanged animal becomes holy

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the new פרק to the main topic of the whole מסכת, which is תמורה.

phrases.english: For items consecrated for the altar create a substitute,

phrases.aramaic: וְקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה.
phrases.english: and items consecrated for Temple upkeep do not create a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first specific example of the general opening line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only קדשי מזבח create a תמורה. קדשי בדק הבית do not.

steps.title: Only Altar Animals Bring Liability for פיגול, נותר, and טומאה
steps.stepSummary: A second difference is that with קדשי מזבח, one is liable for eating under פיגול, נותר, and eating while טמא. The list continues after this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: With altar items, one is liable for eating them because of פיגול, נותר, and eating while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more rules that apply only to קדשי מזבח. The sentence continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three prohibitions come from the laws of קרבנות. Someone who breaks them is liable to כרת. פיגול is a קרבן slaughtered with the plan to eat it after its allowed time. נותר is a קרבן eaten after its time ran out. טמא is eating a קרבן while ritually impure. Things given for Temple upkeep are not eaten as קרבנות, so these prohibitions do not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable, here meaning liable to כרת
A קרבן made invalid by the plan, at the time of the service, to eat it after its allowed time
Meat of a קרבן left over after its allowed time
Ritually impure. Here it means eating a קרבן while impure

phrases.english: With items consecrated for the altar, one is liable for them
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'for it,' in round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets says 'for them.'

phrases.english: because of piggul, notar, and eating while impure,

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל נוֹתָר וְטָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rules that apply only to קדשי מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One is liable for פיגול, נותר, and טמא only with קדשי מזבח.
